thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED — service: redwood-api | severity: P1 | id: INC-2026-0315-01

aj: paging on-call now. saw increased 500s from canary around 00:27 UTC.

aj: oncall here — taking initial triage. pinging infra + runtime.

sam: joining. can you paste the war room link?

incident-bot: War room created: https://warroom.redwood.local/INC-2026-0315-01 (access: eng & infra)

maria: adding product to keep customer comms ready. hit list: PLG storefronts and Dedicated customers in us-east-1.

aj: quick summary: traffic spike -> request latency climbs -> 5xxs start at ~00:27 -> errors concentrated on text-generation route /v1/generate on a subset of hosts in us-east-1.

opsbot: Paging sent to @aj, @lee, @sam (on-call rotation). Escalation timeout set 3m.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered automatically for rollout 2026-03-15_0920 to reduce error rate.

aj: I hit the failing host list:
```
failed_hosts = ["infer-rt-14.use1.redwood", "infer-rt-21.use1.redwood"]
curl -sS infer-rt-14.use1.redwood:9200/health | jq .
{
  "status": "degraded",
  "active_kv": 24,
  "open_streams": 132
}
```

sam: logs show OOM + "cuda: out of memory" traces right before the 500s from infer-rt-21. memory pressure on two GPU nodes.

irene: are we sure it's model-serving memory and not a dependency bump? rolling back the canary makes me think it's runtime stress from traffic pattern.

aj: agreed. mitigation step 1 — mark those hosts as drained from load balancer + spin up replacement nodes from reserved pool. I’m running the drain now.

aj: LB drain command: `rb-lb drain infer-rt-14.use1.redwood --reason "INC-2026-0315-01"`

opsbot: infer-rt-14 removed from rotation. New nodes requested (pool: reserved-dedicated-use1). ETA ~2m.

maria: drafting status page update. suggestion for first public line: 
```
Status: Degraded performance for Redwood API in us-east-1. We are investigating errors affecting some text-generation requests. No data loss reported. More updates to follow.
```

sam: good. let's mark scope: affecting hosted API generation endpoints for ~5% of requests in us-east-1; Dedicated customers on pinned nodes may be affected if pinned to the impacted hosts.

maria: customer notification draft for affected customers: 
```
Subject: Temporary service disruption affecting generation endpoints (us-east-1)
Hi — we’re investigating increased error rates for text-generation requests in us-east-1. Our on-call team is actively mitigating; we expect degraded performance for a subset of traffic. We’ll provide an update in 15 minutes or when we have a root cause.

If you rely on pinned dedicated nodes, check your console for instance health or reach out to support for immediate assistance.

Apologies for the interruption — Redwood Support
```

aj: sending the draft to support for pre-approval, will post status page update now.

incident-bot: Status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0315-01 (initial)

lee: I can take the next 30m triage and keep the war room open while aj coordinates node replacement. please record any config/state changes in the war room log.

aj: handing off to @lee for mitigation runbook step execution. I’ll remain reachable for context.

lee: acknowledged. taking lead. my immediate plan: 1) validate replacement nodes healthy, 2) monitor KV cache behavior, 3) if errors persist, trigger temporary autoscale to add transient capacity, 4) prepare rollback plan for latest model quantization.

sam: one ask — tag any customer notices with incident id and include the ETA if we get it. also note any SLA impact for Dedicated contracts.

maria: noted. will include incident id and a targeted ETA if we have one in the next update.

aj: update — replacement nodes are up and passing health checks; LB will rejoin gradually. immediate 500 rate dropped from ~12% to ~1.8% in last 90s.

maria: posting 15-minute update to status and sending out customer email to affected list.

incident-bot: Update posted: Partial recovery — performance improving in us-east-1; we continue to monitor.

irene: recording RCA checklist: potential causes to track: kernel-level driver memory leak, model KV cache behavior with long prefixes, or a new quantized kernel regression. we should capture GPU metrics + kernel versions from failing hosts.

lee: starting post-incident capture: `rb-capture-metrics --hosts infer-rt-14,infer-rt-21 --since 00:20`

aj: leaving the war room; @lee now primary on-call for this incident. I’ll rejoin if anything changes.

lee: thanks. I'll keep the war room open for 45m then close if stable. please file a follow-up postmortem and assign owner for long-term fix (tag: infra/runtime).

maria: will schedule the follow-up and draft the internal incident comms template for execs.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 1765009110.

lee: closing notes to add to war room before I hand off: root cause investigation in progress, customer notifications sent, status page updated twice, recovery validated. handing to infra team for RCA next steps.

sam: thanks all — good quick mitigation and coordination.

maria: thanks team :heart:
